title: Which letter counts the twentieth object?
description: Objects are counted with the letters of the alphabet in order, and the video finds which letter counts the twentieth object and what happens at the twenty seventh. Then the Roman table gives thirteen and eighteen. Keeko's doubt is that the alphabet can start again after z.
teaching_notes: One idea: counting with letters is a one-to-one match with a fixed order, and it stops when the letters stop. Roman symbols write the next numbers by putting a bigger symbol before smaller ones. Watch for students who restart the alphabet and forget that one letter would then stand for two counts.

source: Using the letters a to z as a counting sequence, which lette
video_script.why: The child sees that a counting sequence with a fixed order stops when its symbols stop, and sees how the Roman table writes the next numbers.
video_script.substitution: Line the objects up and write the letters under them in alphabet order, then read the Roman table for the two numbers.
video_script.anchor: a row of objects with the letters of the alphabet written under them in order, and the Roman table beside them
video_script.wrong_answer: the twenty seventh object gets eigh again
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko starts the alphabet again after z, so the twenty seventh object gets eigh again. Then eigh would stand for both one and twenty seven, so the count is lost.
video_script.payoff_line: The twentieth object is tee, and the letters stop before twenty seven

final_answer.value: The 20th object is t; 27 objects cannot be counted; 13 is XIII and 18 is XVIII
final_answer.spoken: the twentieth object is tee, twenty seven objects cannot be counted, thirteen is ex eye eye eye and eighteen is ex vee eye eye eye

hold_back: The 20th object is t; 27 objects cannot be counted; 13 is XIII and 18 is XVIII
never_show: the answer card before the last beat of the board solution
maths_rules: the letters a, b, c, ..., z count objects 1, 2, 3, ..., 26 in order
the 20th letter of the alphabet is t
the alphabet has only 26 letters, so the 27th object has no letter
13 = 10 + 3, so 13 is X then III: XIII
18 = 10 + 5 + 3, so 18 is X, V, III: XVIII
the Roman symbols read: I is 1, V is 5, X is 10
video_script.design: One idea: letters count in a fixed order and stop at the last letter. The row of objects with letters stays on the stage; the Roman table appears for the last two steps.

<bookmark mark='row'/>Count objects with the letters of the alphabet, in order. Eigh counts the first, bee counts the second, and so on.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which letter counts the twentieth object, and what happens when there are twenty seven objects?

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Join each object to one letter, following the order of the alphabet.
<bookmark mark='name'/>This match is called a one-to-one mapping.
<bookmark mark='table'/>Beside it sits the Roman table, which lists the symbols for one to twenty.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the letter for the twentieth object, and see what happens at twenty seven.
Then we write thirteen and eighteen in Roman symbols.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: match objects with a, b, c, ... in order; the 10th letter is j; the 20th letter is t

marks.m1: the letters run along the objects; the 10th is j and the 20th is t, each marked

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, match the objects with the letters in order.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Counting along, the tenth letter is jay, and the twentieth letter is tee.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the alphabet has 26 letters, so the 27th object has no letter; the sequence runs out after z

marks.m2: the letters stop at z and the 27th object is left with an empty box

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, go on to the twenty seventh object.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The alphabet has only twenty six letters, so this object has no letter. The sequence runs out.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 13 = 10 + 3; in the Roman table, 10 is X and 3 is III, so 13 is XIII

marks.m3: 13 splits into 10 and 3, the table gives X and III, and the two join as XIII

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, read thirteen from the Roman table.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Thirteen is ten and three. Ten is ex, and three is three eyes, so thirteen is ex followed by three eyes.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: 18 = 10 + 5 + 3; in the Roman table, 10 is X, 5 is V and 3 is III, so 18 is XVIII

marks.m4: 18 splits into 10, 5 and 3, the table gives X, V and III, and the three join as XVIII

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, read eighteen from the Roman table.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Eighteen is ten, five and three. Ten is ex, five is vee, and three is three eyes.

beats.on_screen: Answer: The 20th object is t; 27 objects cannot be counted; 13 is XIII and 18 is XVIII

marks.res: the letter t, the empty box, XIII and XVIII glow one after another

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The twentieth object is tee, and the letters stop before twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Twenty seven objects cannot be counted. Thirteen is ex eye eye eye, and eighteen is ex vee eye eye eye.
